routes.summary: Shared path, timestamp and bounded-process helpers
constraints: Keep caller-specific policy outside this leaf crate; timestamp bytes are compatibility contracts.

routes.summary: Wire DTOs, validation and channel vocabulary
constraints: Wire changes need an explicit version and cross-language tests; retained channels are not dead code.

routes.summary: Provider-neutral traits, certainty and framed transport
constraints: Only DefinitelyUnsent permits replay; transport phases advance monotonically.

routes.summary: Session open/resume, history and management
constraints: Only live attachments authorize effects; provider-first failures may be OutcomeUnknown.

routes.summary: Event-sourced reducer, projections and durable snapshots
constraints: Reducer stays pure; observable transitions must preserve replay of existing stores.

routes.summary: Consult/handoff journal, broker and coordinator
constraints: Recover before admission; started effects become unknown and are never replayed.

routes.summary: Codex app-server adapter and event mapping
constraints: Provider CLI owns authentication; preserve protocol-specific refusal and unknown-outcome semantics.

routes.summary: Claude CLI adapter, transcript store and event mapping
constraints: Provider CLI owns authentication; preserve protocol-specific refusal and unknown-outcome semantics.

routes.summary: ACP adapter, Grok/Qwen profiles and OpenCode worker runner
constraints: Provider CLI owns authentication; preserve protocol-specific refusal and unknown-outcome semantics.

routes.summary: Test-only provider replay: recorded Claude/Codex/ACP CLI sessions served to the real adapters, the recorder and its identity scrubber
constraints: Never packaged and never a production dependency. Fixtures are real recordings, scrubbed by the recorder; never hand-write or hand-edit one: re-record (live, opt-in) or re-scrub a kept journal. A real provider turn happens only in the ignored recording test.

routes.summary: Atomic writes, private directories, leases and CAS
constraints: After rename, a failed write is uncertain; never unlink the writer lock or add a second canonical writer.

routes.summary: Session cache, worktrees and checkpoints
constraints: Persisted bytes and checkpoint path policy are contracts; inspect retained surface before removing unused code.

routes.summary: Appearance, saved workspaces, project pins and profile stores
constraints: Rust owns persistence; old appearance versions remain accepted; changed looks need current-session approval.

routes.summary: Colour themes: built-in palettes, theme files in ~/.config/interface/themes, looks (a backdrop behind glass panes and threads, moving scenes), the Settings theme picker
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/renderer/theme-files.test.ts src/renderer/theme-accessibility.test.ts src/renderer/theme-look.test.ts src/renderer/chrome-mode.test.ts src/shared/custom-themes-contract.test.ts
constraints: Built-in palettes change colours and fonts only (settled look); theme files may use any CSS. The token system stays inside @layer interface-palette so a theme file's plain :root rule wins; never !important there. Rust reads theme files and never writes them.

A look's glass rules stay scoped to :root[data-theme-look="backdrop"], so built-in palettes and theme files without a backdrop paint as before. A moving backdrop is stepped at 30 frames a second and rests while Interface is not in front, under Reduce motion, and when Settings turns it off (owner's battery rule); never let its animations run free. A scene is cleaned before it is drawn.

routes.summary: Credential-filtered git diff and bounded check runner
constraints: Do not weaken path filtering or output/deadline bounds; review commands are not arbitrary shell execution.

routes.summary: File search, Quick Open, editor and customization inventory
constraints: Use current workspace authority and compare-and-save identity checks; no symlink or secret reads.

routes.summary: Prompt path grants and pasted image handling
constraints: Grants remain exact and every canonicalization rechecks identity.

routes.summary: PTY lifecycle, generation fences, titles and launch profiles
constraints: Preserve generation fencing and lifecycle lock order; process effects and title authority remain Rust-owned.

routes.summary: Desktop dispatch, workspace grants and checkpoint adapters
constraints: Exactly one owner per operation; error certainty is typed, never inferred from prose.

routes.summary: Update state, feed admission, macOS verification and the public update channel
constraints: Preserve generation-fenced verification and sticky Ready; production install/restart needs owner authority.
Once a build is public: never change the feed address, the manifest file name or schema, or drop every trusted key; publishing is owner-requested (docs/PUBLIC_UPDATES.md).

routes.summary: Voice protocol, sentence chunks and speech cleanup
constraints: Protocol and text projection stay Rust-owned; microphone and real speech tests are separate from unit checks.

routes.summary: Phone access, trust, encrypted connection and relay
constraints: Mac owns trust and input effects; discovery never grants authority; preserve v1-v5 compatibility and replay refusal.

routes.summary: Phone relay on Cloudflare Workers (off-Wi-Fi access)
constraints: Speaks the Mac's v5 relay protocol unchanged (no Mac or phone release); only ciphertext crosses it; deploying needs the owner's Cloudflare account.

routes.summary: Rust desktop adapter, startup and operation routing
constraints: Adapters call Rust domain services; preserve push-before-response order, one writer and typed effect certainty.

routes.summary: iface argv, TUI commands, drawing and terminal lifecycle
constraints: Only main.rs emits process output; sanitize display text and preserve exit-code distinctions and PTY teardown.

routes.summary: Bounded Away pilot, selected-file CLI cycle and one-button project loop
constraints: Demo accepts fresh disposable projects only; recovery never replays uncertain provider or apply effects.
Project loops act only after an owner start; Stop and expiry prevent continuation, and restart never replays work.

A project loop is a Threads thread in its own worktree (protocol 45): it holds the thread while it runs, and the Away store is project-away.v3.json (protocol 47: an optional reviewer) with a read-once v2, else v1, carry-over.

routes.summary: Archived features (Clean GUI, pane delegation, Control assistant, Tailscale phone route) and the wire shims that answer unavailable
constraints: Archived features return only on a new owner instruction. Their channels stay wire protocol and answer unavailable; their data files stay on disk, unread.

routes.summary: Electron lifecycle, sandboxed preload and host transport
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/main/ipc-payload.test.ts src/main/rust-host-client.test.ts
constraints: Preload has no runtime imports; channel changes require Rust, shared TS, encoder, preload and host contract checks.

routes.summary: Sidebar grouping, search, project pins and attention projections
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/renderer/viewmodels.test.ts src/renderer/workspace-ui.test.ts
constraints: Persistent decisions live in interface-settings; read SETTLED_LOOKS before visual changes.

routes.summary: Transcript projections, grouping and Markdown display
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/renderer/conversation-projection.test.ts src/renderer/conversation.test.ts src/renderer/components/Conversation.queue.test.ts src/renderer/draft-store.test.ts src/renderer/markdown.test.ts src/renderer/markdown-incremental.test.ts
constraints: Keep unresolved approvals and pending effects; compare incremental projection with the reference reducer.

routes.summary: Mounted xterm panes, layout, keyboard and accessibility
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/renderer/terminal-workspace.test.ts src/renderer/terminal-splitter-drag.test.ts src/renderer/terminal-announcements.test.ts src/renderer/terminal-stream-router.test.ts src/renderer/terminal-restore-matrix.test.ts
constraints: Keep xterm instances mounted and generation-fenced; layout/interaction changes need the real renderer lane.

routes.summary: Prompt editing, attachments and submission presentation
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/renderer/composer.test.ts src/renderer/composer-model.test.ts src/renderer/prompt-submit.test.ts src/renderer/prompt-context.test.ts src/renderer/outbound-lane.test.ts
constraints: App.tsx alone calls window.iface; unknown outcomes never resend or restore captured context.

routes.summary: Rust-owned agent teammates: roster, threads, home folders, approval policy, routines and run history
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/renderer/agent-roster.test.ts
constraints: Rust persists run claims before provider launch; restart marks active runs Unknown without replay.

routes.summary: Native iPhone library and shared phone conversation
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/remote/native-transport.test.ts

xcodebuild -project apps/interface-ios/InterfacePhone.xcodeproj -scheme InterfacePhone -configuration Debug -destination "platform=iOS Simulator,name=Interface iPhone" -derivedDataPath /private/tmp/interface-ios-build test
constraints: Select an installed Simulator; credentials remain native and Mac authority stays in Rust. Full gate does not replace native/physical acceptance.

routes.summary: Apple speech framework helper and audio buffers
constraints: Swift adapts Apple frameworks; Rust owns voice policy. Self-test speaks audio; it is not part of this focused command.

routes.summary: Navigation, gates, fix proofs, Dev closeout, packaging and release receipts
constraints: `cargo xtask check --changed` gates xtask changes with the Rust suite (`xtask/src/package.rs` also runs Electron's); receipts bind source bytes and each suite's tools, and Dev landing does not authorize production promotion.

routes.summary: Shared command catalog, durable Attention, task results, drafts and bounded pairing experiment
constraints: The Rust host alone writes harness.v1.json. Seen never resolves an Attention event.
Check evidence is immutable and candidate-bound. Draft compare-and-set never sends input.
Pairing is opt-in, bounded and held for explicit decision; pane delegation is retired.

routes.summary: Desktop collaboration request lifetime and durable receipt reconciliation
constraints: Inject host API from App; preserve newer durable receipts and invalidate stale list responses.

routes.summary: Version-bound project output previews and scoped feedback beside native terminals
constraints: Rust rechecks current project authority and file identity; output content cannot invoke the privileged bridge.
Feedback stays bound to the displayed hash; never remount terminals or replay provider input.

routes.summary: Browser pane: the <webview> page, address bar, width presets and point-and-fix (pick an element or mark a region, note and picture into a thread's draft)
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/renderer/browser-point.test.ts src/renderer/browser-pane.test.ts src/main/browser-pane.test.ts src/shared/browser-events.test.ts
cd electron && INTERFACE_BROWSER_POINT_ONLY=1 npm run test:renderer
cd electron && INTERFACE_BROWSER_CHROME_ONLY=1 npm run test:renderer
constraints: The guest and its popups keep no preload, no Node and no IPC, stay in persist:browser-pane and on http(s); permissions are decided in main only as docs/WORKSPACE_TOOLS.md says (camera, microphone, notifications and clipboard read ask once per site for the run, fullscreen, pointer lock and clipboard write allowed, another app asks, the rest refused; the sheet defaults to Block). Downloads go through the injectable folder hook; tests never write to the owner's Downloads.
The picker runs in the page's main world, so its result is untrusted page data: bound and clean it, draw it only as text, and show it before it reaches a draft. Add to draft never sends.

routes.summary: Threads surface: Rust-owned thread inbox state, thread workspaces, per-turn checkpoints, diffs and fork at a turn
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/renderer/thread-card.test.ts src/renderer/thread-turns.test.ts src/renderer/thread-view.test.ts src/renderer/composer-thread.test.ts src/renderer/components/ThreadDiffPanel.test.ts
cd electron && INTERFACE_THREADS_ONLY=1 npm run test:renderer
cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/renderer/thread-inbox.test.ts src/renderer/use-thread-inbox.test.ts src/renderer/components/ThreadInbox.test.ts
constraints: Rust derives every section, unread flag, order key and restore permission; the renderer only renders the ThreadsView and sends commands.

Thread identity is the session key; registry.json stays untouched. Wire changes go through threads-v34.json (threads-v36.json for turn ends, threads-v37.json for shipping) in both languages; threads.v2.json carries threads.v1.json over read-only.
threadControl is never replay-safe as an operation; refusals say definitely-unsent explicitly and git effects never touch the user's index, branch or stash.

routes.summary: Thread journal: each thread's append-only record (prompts, answers, tools, turn ends), the Threads search's In messages, and history for providers that keep none
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/shared/thread-journal.test.ts src/renderer/thread-inbox.test.ts
constraints: The observer does no I/O and never awaits: events, run changes and prompts reach one journal worker over one channel, in pump order.
Only the process holding host.lock writes thread-journal/; readers take no lock and skip what they cannot parse.
iface:threadJournal only reads; the journal's wire and line shapes go through thread-journal-v56.json in both languages.

routes.summary: Team tools: an agent in a thread starts, waits for, reads and messages other threads through the per-session iface_team MCP server
checks: cargo test --locked -p engine-claude -p engine-codex -p engine-acp team_tools
cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/renderer/started-threads.test.ts src/main/handsfree-fake-claude.test.ts src/shared/threads.test.ts
constraints: The caller is the socket it connected to, bound to the session key the provider confirmed; never anything in tool input.
A started thread runs at collaboration depth 1 (also on resume): no team tools, no collaboration MCP, exactly one level.
Permissions never widen: the target engine's mode at the caller's rung or the nearest lower one; no tool input picks a mode.
Starts and sends go through the guarded runtime and the send hook; an unknown outcome is reported and never retried.

routes.summary: Switch provider inside a thread: one thread runs as a chain of provider sessions, handed over from the journal, and switches back with only what was missed
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/renderer/thread-switch.test.ts src/renderer/thread-opinion.test.ts src/main/handsfree-fake-acp.test.ts src/shared/threads.test.ts
constraints: Exactly one segment of a chain is listed (the head); a switch moves the thread's owner-facing state to it in one store commit.
A target that cannot be opened changes nothing; a handoff whose send is unknown stands and is never retried.
A new session never runs wider than the thread: the target's mode at the old head's rung or the nearest lower one.
An earlier segment's turns draw no per-turn control; history for a head with two or more segments comes from the journal.

routes.summary: Scheduled prompts and pull-request watch: a thread is sent a prompt at a time, on a repeat or a calendar, or when its pull request's checks fail or new review comments arrive
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/renderer/thread-schedules.test.ts src/shared/threads.test.ts src/main/handsfree-fake-claude.test.ts
constraints: Each firing is recorded as an attempt (outcome unknown) before its send and is delivered at most once, ever; an unknown outcome is never retried, after a restart included.
Delivery goes through the gate the phone's send uses: idle or failed, no Away loop or Code pane, not settled or archived; a busy thread is waited for, one firing at a time.
Only the latest missed due time fires (never a burst), and only when it is less than a day late.
gh is read only through interface_review's Gh, off the worker, on the pull-request pass.

routes.summary: Resume at reset: when a thread's provider hits its usage limit, the limit line offers Resume at reset (the thread carries on by itself a minute after the reset) and Snooze until reset
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/renderer/thread-resume.test.ts src/shared/threads.test.ts src/main/handsfree-fake-claude.test.ts
constraints: A resume is a one-time scheduled prompt (kind resume, one per thread): the scheduler's gate, occurrence id and one attempt apply unchanged; an unknown outcome is never retried.
Never a guessed time: without a reset from the notice or a full usage window of the thread's own account, neither action is offered and resumeAtReset is refused.
A resume never carries a prompt whose delivery is unknown; a limit-refused prompt goes as a Retry of its prompt-recovery receipt, so it can never go twice.
The provider replay fixtures are real recordings: never edit them.

routes.summary: Several accounts per provider: named Claude, Codex and Grok profile directories, which account each session is bound to, and the account a new thread, terminal pane or sign-in uses
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/shared/provider-accounts.test.ts src/renderer/provider-accounts-view.test.ts
constraints: The Default account is the host's inherited environment: no directory, never removed, and its adapter, environment, store roots and argv are exactly as before accounts.
The account is never part of the session key or the engine id; session-accounts.v1.json binds added-account sessions only.
Sign-in state comes only from each CLI run with the account's environment; nothing reads credentials.
A session bound to a removed account is history that cannot be resumed; resume refuses definitely-unsent.

routes.summary: Composer references and stash: Quote a reply's selection, send a terminal selection to a thread's draft, refer to another thread (Rust writes the block), and stash drafts in Rust
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/shared/draft-stash.test.ts src/renderer/composer-quote.test.ts src/renderer/thread-reference.test.ts src/renderer/draft-stash-view.test.ts
constraints: Rust alone decides what another thread's block holds and whether the sender may read it (team tools' may_read, through heads); whatever the renderer sends as a chat item's safeContent is ignored.
Selected text, terminal output and other threads' words are plain text: bounded, never rendered as HTML, placed in a prompt as quoted data.
A stash keeps references only; a stashed draft's file paths keep pasted images but grant nothing, and restored paths are granted again.
A stash belongs to the thread: it follows a switched thread's head and is forgotten with the thread.

routes.summary: Quick wins: Write with AI for commit messages and pull request text, the private secret card (request_secret), and side questions (/btw)
checks: cargo test --locked -p interface-host -- write_with_ai a_given_secret a_side_question
cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/shared/thread-secrets.test.ts src/renderer/thread-ship.test.ts src/renderer/thread-secrets.test.ts src/renderer/side-question.test.ts
constraints: A given secret's value exists only in its 0600 file: never in a tool result, push, journal, store, draft or log; the channel's payload is never logged.
Write with AI reads only through thread_git::diff (credential and binary files named, not read) and redacts what it quotes; it commits and pushes nothing.
A side thread is never a thread record: it is hidden, resumes one hop down with no team tools, and is deleted when closed or with its thread.

routes.summary: Saved project setup readiness and reusable thread recipes
constraints: Only explicitly saved setup runs; failed/interrupted setup never yields a launch token and is never replayed automatically.
Recipes store context descriptors, not cached file bytes or credentials; ordinary context authority still validates at launch.

routes.summary: Visual replies: an agent shows a rendered page above its reply through team tools' show_visual, kept per thread and drawn only in a sandboxed iface-visual: frame
checks: cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/shared/visual-frame.test.ts src/main/visual-frames.test.ts src/main/visual-network-fence.test.ts src/renderer/visual-reply.test.ts
cd electron && INTERFACE_RENDERER_LANE=visual-reply npm run test:renderer
constraints: A visual page is drawn only in <iframe sandbox="allow-scripts"> on an iface-visual: URL that main serves with the visual CSP and sandbox headers; never srcdoc, blob: or data: (they inherit the app policy), never allow-same-origin.
The app CSP frames only iface-visual:, and a frame showing a visual never navigates; no postMessage listener exists for a visual.

WebRTC is outside CSP: the app window keeps disable_non_proxied_udp and its session a proxy that leads nowhere, loopback included (visual-network-fence.ts); the window itself makes no network request.
Pages are at most 512 KiB, 64 and 16 MiB a thread, owner-private, removed with their session; the event never carries the page.

routes.summary: Outside agents: a Claude Code or Codex running outside Interface lists, reads and (when the owner allows it) starts and messages Interface threads through iface mcp and the host's owner-only outside socket
checks: cargo build --locked -p iface && cargo test --locked -p interface-host --test suite outside_agents
cd electron && npx --no-install vitest run src/renderer/outside-agents.test.ts src/shared/threads.test.ts src/renderer/components/SettingsPage.test.ts
constraints: Off by default; the level is the owner's Settings choice, kept in the team tools ledger (never the Threads store) and read at every call.
The outside socket is 0600 in a 0700 directory and the host drops a peer whose uid is not its own; iface mcp talks only to a socket and directory its own user owns.
The caller is the connection the host accepted; no tool input names a caller, a level, a mode or a folder. A start names an existing Interface project's root or name only.

A started thread runs at the target's asking rung (child_mode(engine, Rung::Ask)) at collaboration depth 1 with no team tools, on the provider's default account; 4 running and 16 in all per outside session, 64 a day across sessions.
Read can change nothing; send and stop reach only threads that outside session started. A call lost after it reached the host is outcome-unknown, never retried.
